Backend: 11/12 pytest pass + 1 skip (no auto-fixable balance/integrity alert currently in the workshop; dry-run test self-skipped as designed). /api/firewall/dashboard returns health.score=70 status=متوسط, 10 alerts (1 critical duplicate + 8 consistency + 1 anomaly), cash_flow.net=-10908.5, 8-key health breakdown, stats (journals=57, ops=61, visits=102) and live_activity. Filters by severity=critical and category=duplicate_detection both narrow correctly. Dismiss writes firewall_dismissed_alerts with expires_at; Resolve writes firewall_resolved_alerts and also upserts a permanent dismissal. AI insights: ai_enabled=false when use_ai=false (rules-only); ai_enabled flag returned correctly when use_ai=true (Emergent LLM key path active, no exception). Frontend: route /accounting/firewall renders the new FirewallPanel — HealthScoreGauge shows score 70, status متوسط, breakdown grid visible; all 8 KPI cards render (critical/high/inflow/outflow/journals/visits/cashflow/insights); AIInsightsPanel + LiveActivityFeed render; 10 alert-card-* elements present; all 5 severity filters + 6 category filters present and FUNCTIONAL (severity=critical → 1 card; category=consistency → 8 cards); AlertDetailsDrawer opens on 'التفاصيل' click and displays evidence/auto_fix_preview content. 0 console errors during full UI walkthrough.

minor.issue: Auto-fix dry_run was SKIPPED because no balance_integrity or integrity (orphan) alert with auto_fix=='auto' currently exists in this workshop. The skip is correct (no auto-fixable target), not a bug — but coverage of the actual dry-run preview branches (would_delete / would_create_adjustment) cannot be proven against the live DB. Seed an unbalanced or orphan journal to verify in next iteration.

action_items: (Optional) Seed one synthetic orphan journal (source='operation_cogs' with reference_id pointing to a deleted op) so the auto-fix dry_run can be exercised end-to-end against the live API (currently skipped).

(Optional, perf) /api/firewall/dashboard takes ~30s on first call because it scans 2000+ journal_entries + 5000+ operations + 5000+ visits per request. The frontend masks this via the 'firewall-loading' screen but users will feel it on the very first paint. Consider (a) Redis-cache the analysis for ~30s, or (b) push run_full_analysis to a background scheduler and serve the last snapshot. Not blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: firewall_engine.FirewallEngine.run_full_analysis() is called from EVERY endpoint (dashboard, health-score, alerts, alert detail, auto-fix, live-activity, ai-insights) — each call re-fetches all 3 large tables from Supabase. The engine has a _cache dict but it's scoped per-instance, and every endpoint constructs a NEW engine, so the cache is never reused across requests. This is the source of the ~30s first-call latency. RECOMMEND: introduce a module-level TTL cache keyed by workshop_id, OR have routes_firewall.py build the engine once and reuse it within a single request (engine is already a singleton per request, but multi-endpoint frontend dashboard hits dashboard+ai-insights in parallel = 2× full scans).

routes_firewall.firewall_auto_fix raises HTTPException(400) when DB_PROVIDER != 'supabase', but the Mongo path is never implemented. Today's workshop runs on Supabase so it works, but the dependency on provider==supabase is silent. Add a clearer error message or implement a Mongo branch.

firewall_engine.detect_suspicious_entries iterates only the first 200 journals (`self._journals()[:200]`) — but the order is desc by created_at, so it's the 200 most-recent, which is reasonable. Document this 200 cap in the docstring so future maintainers know detection is windowed.

FirewallPanel.jsx loads dashboard AND ai-insights in parallel on mount and on every 'finance:updated' event — each is ~30s on first call. Consider serializing (dashboard first, insights only after) or debouncing finance:updated.
